subject: Cigarette smoking
passage_locator: CDC Health Effects of Cigarettes: Cardiovascular Disease → Smoking and cardiovascular disease → Smoking can → Damage cells that line the blood vessels; Increase the buildup of plaque in blood vessels; Cause thickening and narrowing of blood vessels.
support_summary: CDC explicitly identifies cigarette smoking as contributing to vascular injury and increased atherosclerotic plaque accumulation. The relationship is supported as contributory causation rather than an inevitable outcome. Smoking is not the sole cause of atherosclerosis.
source_title: Health Effects of Cigarettes: Cardiovascular Disease
web_scope_caution: Direct mechanistic support for a contributory effect; not an inevitable outcome.

subject: Lung tissue injury and scarring
passage_locator: Ravimohan et al. Tuberculosis and lung damage: from epidemiology to pathophysiology → Table 1 → Pulmonary cavitation; Pulmonary fibrosis; Pulmonary impairment after TB → Variability in lung function deficits → Airflow obstruction; Restrictive ventilatory defects.
support_summary: The review documents structural lung abnormalities including cavitation fibrosis and bronchiectasis following pulmonary tuberculosis. These changes are associated with persistent airflow obstruction restrictive ventilatory defects and impaired gas exchange. Structural remodeling is approved as a contributor to pulmonary impairment after tuberculosis. However observational findings and incomplete mechanistic understanding do not establish independent causality. ASSOCIATED_WITH is the supported relation.
source_title: Tuberculosis and lung damage: from epidemiology to pathophysiology
web_scope_caution: Post-TB lung scarring/fibrosis is associated with persistent impairment; ASSOCIATED_WITH is appropriate, not CAUSES from observational evidence.

subject: Persistent high blood pressure
passage_locator: NHLBI High Blood Pressure → Symptoms → Learn About the Effects of High Blood Pressure → Video description stating that high blood pressure damages artery walls over time.
support_summary: NHLBI explicitly identifies arterial wall damage over time as an effect of high blood pressure. The approved direction from persistent hypertension to arterial injury is supported as a possible causal process. The cited description does not establish a specific cerebral vascular mechanism or imply equal injury in all patients.
web_scope_caution: Supports progressive vascular injury; page is an independently found related NHLBI source, not the exact video cited in the original locator.

subject: Arterial wall damage
passage_locator: American Stroke Association → How High Blood Pressure Can Lead to Stroke → Stroke and high blood pressure; What happens when you have a stroke.
support_summary: The American Stroke Association explains that high blood pressure damages arteries and increases their susceptibility to blockage or rupture. Weakened or blocked cerebral arteries increase the likelihood of ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke. Arterial injury is therefore supported as a stroke risk factor rather than a sufficient or deterministic cause. RISK_FACTOR_FOR is retained.
source_title: How High Blood Pressure Can Lead to Stroke
web_scope_caution: Primary source establishes high blood pressure to stroke risk through arterial damage, not a separately measured independent risk from arterial wall damage alone.

subject: coronary artery disease
passage_locator: CDC About Coronary Artery Disease → Symptoms → Over time CAD can weaken the heart muscle; Causes → Coronary plaque accumulation and reduced myocardial blood flow.
support_summary: CDC directly explains that coronary artery disease can weaken heart muscle over time. Coronary plaque can reduce myocardial blood supply and coronary obstruction may cause myocardial injury. This supports coronary artery disease as a possible cause of heart muscle weakening or damage. Not every patient with CAD develops myocardial injury or heart failure.
web_scope_caution: Supports possible myocardial weakening through coronary obstruction and ischemia.

subject: Heart muscle damage or weakening
passage_locator: NHLBI Heart Failure Causes and Risk Factors → What causes left-sided heart failure? → Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction → Chronic conditions that damage or weaken heart muscles.
support_summary: NHLBI identifies chronic damage or weakening of heart muscle as a major cause of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Reduced ventricular contractile capacity can impair cardiac pumping and lead to heart failure. The relationship is a supported causal pathway particularly for HFrEF and does not imply that all heart failure develops through the same mechanism.
source_title: Heart Failure - Causes and Risk Factors
web_scope_caution: Direct for reduced-EF heart failure; this is not a universal heart-failure mechanism.

subject: Excess adiposity
passage_locator: NIDDK Insulin Resistance and Prediabetes → Who is more likely to develop insulin resistance or prediabetes? → Overweight obesity or large waist size listed as risk factors.
support_summary: NIDDK explicitly identifies overweight obesity and increased waist circumference as factors that raise the likelihood of insulin resistance. Excess adiposity is therefore supported as a risk factor rather than an inevitable cause. RISK_FACTOR_FOR is retained.
web_scope_caution: NIDDK lists overweight, obesity, large waist; risk-factor wording appropriate.

subject: Insulin resistance
passage_locator: NIDDK Symptoms and Causes of Diabetes → What causes type 2 diabetes? → Insulin resistance combined with insufficient pancreatic insulin production and subsequent elevated blood glucose.
support_summary: NIDDK explains that type 2 diabetes develops when impaired insulin action is accompanied by inadequate pancreatic insulin production to maintain normal blood glucose. Insulin resistance contributes to increased risk of type 2 diabetes but is not sufficient on its own. Pancreatic beta-cell compensation can delay or prevent progression. RISK_FACTOR_FOR is retained.
web_scope_caution: Insulin resistance contributes with insufficient insulin output; alone it does not cause inevitable diabetes.

subject: Chronic high blood glucose
passage_locator: NIDDK Diabetic Kidney Disease → How does diabetes cause kidney disease? → High blood glucose can damage blood vessels in the kidneys and damaged vessels do not function as effectively.
support_summary: NIDDK directly establishes that elevated blood glucose can damage renal blood vessels and impair their function. Diabetes-related kidney damage often develops gradually over many years. The relationship is supported as contributory causation and does not imply inevitable kidney injury.
web_scope_caution: NIDDK directly identifies high glucose as damaging renal blood vessels.

subject: Inhaled allergens in susceptible individuals
passage_locator: NHLBI Asthma Causes and Triggers → How asthma affects the lungs → Inhaled pollen or mold may trigger a strong immune response that creates inflammation in susceptible individuals.
support_summary: NHLBI explicitly describes inhaled allergens provoking inflammatory immune responses in susceptible individuals. This supports the causal direction from allergen exposure to airway inflammation. It does not establish that allergens inevitably cause inflammation or initiate chronic asthma in every exposed individual.
web_scope_caution: Source supports allergen-triggered inflammation in predisposed individuals.

subject: Airway inflammation
passage_locator: NHLBI Asthma Attack → Introduction → Asthma attacks occur when swelling or tightening narrows the airways and breathing symptoms worsen; How asthma affects the lungs → Inflammatory airway swelling and narrowing.
support_summary: NHLBI establishes that inflammatory airway swelling contributes to airway narrowing during asthma exacerbations. Inflammation is a contributory mechanism alongside bronchoconstriction and mucus production. This supports the approved causal direction without establishing inflammation as the sole or sufficient cause of every asthma attack.
web_scope_caution: Source describes inflammation/swelling during attacks, not proof that generic inflammation alone initiates a distinct asthma exacerbation. Narrow to contributes to airway narrowing/severity.

subject: Longstanding high blood pressure
object: Damage and narrowing of kidney blood vessels
passage_locator: NIDDK High Blood Pressure and Kidney Disease → How does high blood pressure affect the kidneys? → High blood pressure can constrict and narrow blood vessels including renal vessels and eventually damage and weaken them.
support_summary: NIDDK directly establishes that high blood pressure can cause renal vascular narrowing and damage over time. The narrowing reduces blood flow and vascular injury can compromise kidney function. The relationship is supported as a progressive causal mechanism rather than an inevitable outcome of hypertension.
web_scope_caution: Source supports vascular constriction, narrowing and injury.

subject: Damage and narrowing of kidney blood vessels
passage_locator: NIDDK High Blood Pressure and Kidney Disease → How does high blood pressure affect the kidneys? → Narrowed renal blood vessels reduce blood flow and damaged vessels impair the kidneys' ability to remove wastes and extra fluid.
support_summary: NIDDK directly links renal vascular narrowing and damage with impaired kidney function and reduced removal of waste and excess fluid. This supports renal vascular injury as a possible cause of impaired kidney filtration. Persistent damage may contribute to chronic kidney disease but impaired filtration alone does not establish CKD without evidence of chronicity.
web_scope_caution: Source links renal vessel damage to impaired removal of waste/fluids.

subject: Atrial fibrillation
passage_locator: American Heart Association Why Atrial Fibrillation Matters → How does AFib lead to stroke? → Ineffective atrial contraction causes incomplete emptying and blood pooling in the atria which increases the likelihood of clot formation.
support_summary: The American Heart Association directly explains that atrial fibrillation can cause blood pooling within the atria and increase the likelihood of atrial thrombus formation. RISK_FACTOR_FOR is appropriate because clot formation is possible rather than inevitable in patients with AFib.
web_scope_caution: AFib increases the chance of atrial pooling/clots, not inevitable thrombosis.

subject: Atrial thrombus formation
passage_locator: American Heart Association Why Atrial Fibrillation Matters → How does AFib lead to stroke? → A clot formed in the atria may travel to the brain and obstruct a cerebral artery resulting in embolic ischemic stroke.
support_summary: The American Heart Association directly describes how an atrial thrombus can embolize to the brain and block a cerebral artery causing cardioembolic ischemic stroke. This supports a conditional causal pathway requiring embolization and cerebral arterial obstruction. Atrial thrombus formation alone does not inevitably produce stroke.
web_scope_caution: Conditional cause only when a clot embolizes and occludes brain artery; not every atrial clot causes stroke.

subject: Traumatic brain injury
object: Structural brain injury and epileptogenic remodeling
passage_locator: Pease et al. Insights into epileptogenesis from post-traumatic epilepsy → Introduction → Risk factors for PTE → Epileptogenesis in PTE → Mechanisms → Figure 2 → Traumatic injury followed by neural damage and epileptogenic circuit reorganization.
support_summary: The review identifies TBI as an initiating insult that can cause structural brain injury and initiate epileptogenic remodeling. Mechanisms include neuronal injury neuroinflammation blood-brain barrier dysfunction gliosis and abnormal neural circuit reorganization. Much of the detailed mechanistic evidence comes from preclinical models. Not all traumatic brain injuries progress to epileptogenesis.
source_title: Insights into epileptogenesis from post-traumatic epilepsy
web_scope_caution: Review describes plausible TBI-driven epileptogenic reorganization, often informed by animal models; the compound target combines immediate structural injury with non-universal remodeling.

subject: Structural brain injury and epileptogenic remodeling
passage_locator: Pease et al. Insights into epileptogenesis from post-traumatic epilepsy → Risk factors for PTE → Epileptogenesis in PTE → Mechanisms → Figure 2 → Structural injury and abnormal neural circuitry associated with later unprovoked seizures.
support_summary: The review establishes that structural brain injury and epileptogenic network remodeling contribute to increased susceptibility to post-traumatic epilepsy. The process involves a latency period followed by spontaneous unprovoked seizures. Early provoked seizures within seven days must be distinguished from late post-traumatic seizures. The review recognizes that one late unprovoked seizure can satisfy the PTE definition because recurrence risk is high. RISK_FACTOR_FOR is retained because progression is not inevitable.
source_title: Insights into epileptogenesis from post-traumatic epilepsy
web_scope_caution: Mechanistic review supports a risk pathway, not deterministic PTE. Nature full page required a sign-in in this check; PubMed abstract available.

subject: Respiratory pathogen infection of the alveoli
object: Alveolar immune inflammation with fluid or pus
passage_locator: NHLBI Pneumonia Causes and Risk Factors → Introduction → Respiratory germs enter the lungs and trigger immune responses; inflammation of alveoli can result in accumulation of fluid or pus.
support_summary: NHLBI directly describes respiratory pathogens entering the lungs and activating immune cells that cause alveolar inflammation. Inflammatory responses can fill the alveoli with fluid or pus. This supports the approved causal direction as a recognized pneumonia mechanism. The extent of inflammation and exudate formation varies by pathogen and individual.
web_scope_caution: Source directly describes infection triggering alveolar immune inflammation and accumulation of fluid or pus.

subject: Chronic psychological stress
passage_locator: NHLBI Insomnia Causes and Risk Factors → Stress → Stress or worrying about work school relationships money or bereavement increases the risk of insomnia.
support_summary: NHLBI explicitly identifies psychological stress and persistent worrying as risk factors for insomnia. The relationship supports increased susceptibility to insomnia or sleep disruption but does not establish a specific chronic-stress duration threshold. Stress does not inevitably produce insomnia. RISK_FACTOR_FOR is retained.
web_scope_caution: Source supports stress as an insomnia risk factor but does not specify a necessary chronic-duration threshold.

subject: Insomnia
passage_locator: Li et al. Insomnia and the risk of depression: a meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies → PubMed Abstract → Methods and Results → 34 prospective cohort studies with 172077 participants; pooled RR 2.27 and 95 percent CI 1.89 to 2.71.
support_summary: The prospective meta-analysis found that insomnia was associated with increased risk of subsequent depression across 34 cohort studies involving 172077 participants. The pooled relative risk was 2.27 with substantial heterogeneity of I-squared 92.6 percent and evidence of publication bias. This supports insomnia as a prospective risk factor rather than proof of an independent causal effect. RISK_FACTOR_FOR is retained.
source_title: Insomnia and the Risk of Depression: A Meta-analysis of Prospective Cohort Studies
web_scope_caution: Precise cohort count, sample and RR supported. Severe between-study heterogeneity (I2 92.6%) and publication bias; association is not a causal proof.

subject: Prolonged tobacco smoke exposure
passage_locator: NCI Lung Cancer Prevention Health Professional Version → Risk Factors → Factors Associated With Increased Risk of Lung Cancer → Cigarette smoking → Chronic tobacco carcinogen exposure causes genetic damage and smoking is associated with DNA adduct formation in human lung tissue.
support_summary: NCI directly links chronic exposure to cigarette smoke carcinogens with genetic damage and DNA adduct formation in human lung tissue. This supports prolonged tobacco smoke exposure as a contributor to DNA damage in lung cells. DNA adduct formation does not necessarily establish persistent oncogenic mutations because DNA lesions may be repaired or eliminated.
source_title: Lung Cancer Prevention (PDQ) - Health Professional Version
web_scope_caution: Supports smoke exposure-related DNA damage; not all lesions persist or yield mutations.

subject: DNA damage in lung cells
passage_locator: NCI Lung Cancer Prevention Health Professional Version → The Biology of Carcinogenesis → Initiation promotion and progression; Risk Factors → Cigarette smoking → Tobacco carcinogen-induced genetic damage and DNA adduct formation in human lung tissue contribute to multistep lung carcinogenesis.
support_summary: NCI identifies chronic tobacco carcinogen-associated genetic injury as a driving mechanism in multistep lung carcinogenesis. DNA damage in lung cells can contribute to increased lung cancer susceptibility through accumulated relevant alterations. Initial DNA damage alone is insufficient to establish malignancy and may be repaired. RISK_FACTOR_FOR is appropriate for the specified intermediate relationship.
source_title: Lung Cancer Prevention (PDQ) - Health Professional Version
web_scope_caution: Supports mutation-associated carcinogenesis, but a generic DNA-damage intermediate alone is neither sufficient nor an independently calibrated clinical cancer-risk prediction.

subject: Autoimmune attack on the thyroid in Hashimoto disease
object: Inflammation and damage to thyroid tissue
passage_locator: NIDDK Hashimoto's Disease → What is Hashimoto's disease? → Immune antibodies attack the thyroid gland; white blood cells accumulate in the gland and thyroid tissue becomes damaged.
support_summary: NIDDK directly establishes that Hashimoto disease involves autoimmune attack against thyroid tissue with antibody production immune-cell accumulation and glandular damage. The inflammatory component is supported by thyroiditis and immune-cell infiltration. This supports the causal direction while the degree of tissue injury varies across patients.
web_scope_caution: Source supports autoimmune attack with infiltration and gland injury.

subject: Inflammation and damage to thyroid tissue
passage_locator: NIDDK Hashimoto's Disease → What is Hashimoto's disease? → Thyroid damage reduces hormone production; What are the symptoms of Hashimoto's disease? → Progressive tissue damage and development of hypothyroidism.
support_summary: NIDDK establishes that autoimmune thyroid inflammation and tissue damage can impair thyroid hormone production and lead to hypothyroidism. Hashimoto disease may initially occur with normal thyroid hormone levels and progression to hypothyroidism is not inevitable at every stage. The approved causal direction is supported as a possible disease progression pathway.
web_scope_caution: Direct support for progressive thyroid injury impairing hormone production; not all early-stage Hashimoto cases are hypothyroid.
